enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
1049 AM MST Tue Nov 24 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 1046 AM MST Tue Nov 24 2026

 - Dry with very little chance of rain for the rest of this week
   and through the weekend.

 - Chilly overnight lows tonight; daytime temperatures remaining a
   bit below normal through Thanksgiving, then warming to above
   normal for the weekend.
 
&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1046 AM MST Tue Nov 24 2026

Upper ridge building in nicely over the Desert Southwest this
morning, ahead of an advancing upper trough over the Gulf of
Alaska and west coast of the US. Strong sub-tropical jet persists
over the southern Baja and central Mexico. Dry with cool
temperatures continuing today and Wednesday under the upper ridge.
Southern Dona Ana County will be close to freezing tonight but
decided to leave out of a warning at this time. 

Thursday and Friday...west coast upper trough continues to
decelerate as it moves inland due to sluggish upper low over the
central US/Great Lakes. Trough reaches Arizona Thursday and closes
off a low over the southern Baja. The low is able to tap into some
of the sub-tropical moisture as the main sub-tropical jet moves
off to the east. This moisture is able to make it as far north as
northern Mexico before the northerly winds spilling through the
ridge north of the low end any hopes of moisture getting up to
our area. Thus other than a few high clouds, this system looks to
have little impact on the CWA. 

Saturday into next week...upper ridge behind the exiting low will
dominate Saturday and Sunday...clearing any clouds from the sky
and allowing temperatures to warm back above normal. Next Pacific
trough sweeps through well to our north Sunday night. Little or
no chance for any precipitation. Could be a wind maker but right
now the timing of the trough coming through Sunday night is not
conducive to strong winds. Both Sunday and Monday on the breezy
side but no impactful winds. A change of the trough timing could
change this though. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(18Z TAFS)
Issued at 1046 AM MST Tue Nov 24 2026

VFR conditions through the period with SKC-SCT250. Winds
east/northeast 7-10 knots becoming variable AOB 7 knots this
evening. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1046 AM MST Tue Nov 24 2026

Little in the way of fire concerns for the week ahead. Little
chance for rain through the beginning of next week. Min humidity
remaining above typical levels through this period, and no
significant winds other than some afternoon breezes Sunday and
Monday. Temperatures will stay a bit below normal through
Thanksgiving, then warm to above normal this weekend. 

Min RH: Lowlands 30-40% Wednesday/Thursday, decreasing to 20-30%
Friday through Sunday. Mountains 25-40% through Sunday. Vent rates
generally poor through Friday, becoming fair-good Saturday through
Monday.
